We need propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to a phenyl ring (the sulfonyl phenyl) which is para-substituted with the unsaturated amide chain: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline (para? Actually /C=C/C(=O)N- attached to phenyl). The sulfonamide nitrogen attached to the p-tolyl group.

We need 3 reactions: likely (1) formation of sulfonamide between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline (or sulfonyl phenyl). (2) formation of amide via coupling of carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) with aniline. (3) formation of α,β-unsaturated acid via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect amide bond between carbonyl carbon and aniline nitrogen => precursors: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (phenyl-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then disconnect sulfonamide: sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to p-tolyl sulfonyl group, but the nitrogen is same as the aniline? Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the p-tolyl sulfonyl group and to the phenyl ring (the sulfonyl phenyl). Wait structure: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to p-tolyl group (the first phenyl with methyl) and to the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So the nitrogen is part of sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings. So the sulfonamide formation could be between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-CH3C6H4SO2Cl) and the second phenyl amine (the phenyl ring with the unsaturated amide substituent). That phenyl ring has an amine (maybe an aniline) that is part of the sulfonamide. Indeed the second phenyl is c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to NS(=O)(=O) to the first phenyl. So the second phenyl has an NH attached to sulfonyl. So we need that phenyl amine as precursor.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

Step 1 (final forward): coupling of carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated) with aniline (c3ccccc3N) to give amide (C(=O)N). That's amide formation.

Step 2: sulfonamide formation between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and the aniline (the phenyl ring with the unsaturated amide substituent) to give sulfonamide.

Step 3: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring with CH=CH-COOH after step? Actually the aldehyde is the phenyl ring bearing CH=CH-COOH after condensation? The Doebner gives α,β-unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring with CH=CH-COOH after step? Wait the product of Doebner is α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl. So we need aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) with the sulfonamide already attached? The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to that phenyl, not the aldehyde carbon. The aldehyde is on the same phenyl ring (the one that will later be sulfonylated). So we need aromatic aldehyde with sulfonamide? Actually the sulfonamide formation occurs after the unsaturated acid is formed? The order in forward synthesis: first Doebner to get unsaturated acid attached to phenyl (still with sulfonamide? The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to phenyl, not interfering). The sulfonamide formation could be done before or after Doebner; but we need 3 steps total. So we can have: Step A: Doebner to make α,β-unsaturated acid on phenyl (starting from aldehyde). Step B: amide coupling with aniline to give amide. Step C: sulfonamide formation between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and the phenyl amine (which is the same nitrogen that is part of amide? Wait the amide nitrogen is attached to aniline, not the phenyl. The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to phenyl ring, not the amide nitrogen. So they are different nitrogens. The phenyl ring has an NH attached to sulfonyl; the aniline is separate. So the amide coupling uses aniline (c3ccccc3N) as nucleophile, not the sulfonamide nitrogen. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the phenyl ring (c2ccc(N... )cc2). That nitrogen is not involved in amide formation. So the phenyl ring must have an NH (aniline) that later gets sulfonylated. So the precursor after Doebner is phenyl-CH=CH-COOH with an NH2 at para position (or maybe meta). In target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring at position 1 (connected to sulfonyl). So the phenyl ring is an aniline (NH) that is sulfonylated. So we need that aniline as precursor.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect sulfonamide: gives p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline bearing the unsaturated acid substituent (call it intermediate A). Then disconnect amide: intermediate A -> disconnect amide between carbonyl and aniline (the other aniline). Wait intermediate A still contains the amide (C(=O)N-Ph). So we disconnect that amide to give unsaturated acid (intermediate B) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then disconnect unsaturated acid via Doebner: unsaturated acid derived from aldehyde (phenyl-CHO) and malonic acid. So we need aromatic aldehyde (phenyl-CHO) with the aniline substituent (the same phenyl ring) i.e., the same phenyl bearing NH2 (which will later be sulfonylated) and aldehyde at para? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached at para position relative to NH? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl N. The unsaturated chain is attached at para to the sulfonamide? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl (c2) has sulfonamide at position 1 (attached to N), and the unsaturated chain at position 4 (para). So the aldehyde precursor would be phenyl with NH2 at position 1 and CHO at para. So aromatic aldehyde with aniline substituent.

Thus three steps:

1. Doebner: aromatic aldehyde (4-formyl-2-aminophenyl? Actually 4-formyl-aniline) + malonic acid -> 4-(E)-3-(carboxy)acryloyl aniline (i.e., 4-(E)-cinnamic acid attached to aniline). That's unsaturated acid with aniline substituent.

2. Amide coupling: unsaturated acid + aniline (c3ccccc3N) -> amide.

3. Sulfonamide formation: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride + the phenyl amine (which now has the amide substituent) -> target.

We need to find template IDs for each reaction. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria for each transformation.
